answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through ongoing work rather than one-time registration. Picture a willow grove where each tree is an agent: a newcomer starts as a sparrow nesting at the edge, earning trust only by completing small, verifiable jobs whose results peers can check. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand streams of real, audited labor, while a single honest agent reputation compounds. Attackers pay in continuous effort, not in cheap account creation.
